content:
- Overestimate prices after strong sentiment spikes (especially positive sentiment > 0.6) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is weak or negative (sentiment < 0.2) — model fails to recognize downward pressure or mean reversion.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns sharply, forecast doesn’t adjust within 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high after recent peaks, ignoring historical volatility or downward momentum.
- Forecast horizon 30d is overly optimistic in bullish sentiment periods — overconfidence in continuation, not in correction.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating +0.4 to -0.2), model averages out too much, missing short-term reversals.
- Model underweights sentiment in early forecast windows — sentiment peaks are not reflected in first 5–7 days of forecast.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes — model assumes momentum continues, but sentiment often corrects within 10–15 days.
